It was a warm,sunny day on the Agalega Islands, about 600 miles north of mainland Mauritius. 8 year old Mathieu watched as a plane soared overhead, leaving the Vingt Cinq airstrip and heading for Rodrigues. He hated biology, it was the reason why he was sitting on the beach right now. He had been sent home by Mr Thuram for causing constant disruption in the the classroom. 'It's not my fault, his lessons shouldn't be so boring. I don't care about cells and microscopes, biology should be about animals' he thought to himself. He looked at his plastic spiderman watch. The face read 2:17 PM. He sighed and went back to laying in the soft, white sand.

Mathieu's mind turned to going home. He couldn't leave yet, otherwise his dad would find out about his run in with Mr Thuram. That is if the school hadn't already rang him. His dad was a stern man who you didn't want to cross. Being a simple fisherman with little income had made Mathieu's want him to succeed, and the best way to do that was to get a good education and move to the mainland. If this meant that Mathieu had to be given tough love to get there, then that is what would happen. Mathieu didn't see it this way though. He did whatever he could to avoid his father. Vingt Cinq wasn't the most exciting place for a young boy to grow up in. Even the name of the town was no fun, named after the number of lashes a slave would be given as punishment. He often came to the beach, he liked to watch the geckos skate along the sand as if it was ice. Mathieu laid his head back onto the banking and stared at the clouds. His eyes began to grow and he drifted off to sleep.

He awoke with a start as the roar of an airplane flew past. He sat up sharply. As he wiped the sleep from his eyes, he noticed his watch once more. It was now 3:54. Mathieu jumped up and grabbed his bag. He was going to be late home and then his dad would definitely know there had been an incident. He was just about to leave when something caught his eye. Something was glinting in the sun. Taking a step back towards the sea, he could see an object at the edge of the water. As he walked towards the ocean, he could make out that the object was a glass bottle. When he bent down to grab it, he saw a rolled up piece of paper inside.

Mathieu unscrewed the lid and took the paper from inside. He opened the rolled up scrap of paper. He saw what appeared to be a letter of some kind. The paper seemed to be wet, as if there was a slight opening in the bottle. This had caused the ink to smudge and become blurred. Mathieu could only make out a few words and letters.
